name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER12_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequence of intermediate compounds in glycolysis

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following intermediate metabolites formed during glycolysis in the correct sequential order starting from glucose:

  1. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate
  2. 3-Phosphoglyceric acid
  3. Glucose-6-phosphate
  4. Phosphoenolpyruvate
  5. 1,3-Bisphosphoglyceric acid

Choose the correct sequence from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glycolysis is a sequential metabolic pathway consisting of ten enzyme-catalyzed reactions occurring in the cytoplasm, wherein one molecule of glucose undergoes partial oxidation to yield two molecules of pyruvic acid.

Step 2: Sequential Step-by-Step Analysis of Intermediate Formation
1. Glucose is initially phosphorylated by hexokinase to form Glucose-6-phosphate (III).
2. Glucose-6-phosphate isomerises to fructose-6-phosphate, which is subsequently phosphorylated by phosphofructokinase to produce Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (I).
3. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is cleaved into triose phosphates, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (PGAL) and dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP). PGAL is then oxidized and phosphorylated to form 1,3-Bisphosphoglyceric acid (V).
4. 1,3-Bisphosphoglyceric acid loses a phosphate group via substrate-level phosphorylation to yield 3-Phosphoglyceric acid (II).
5. 3-Phosphoglyceric acid is converted to 2-phosphoglycerate and dehydrated to form Phosphoenolpyruvate (IV), which finally yields pyruvic acid.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
Tracking each compound in order of emergence gives: Glucose-6-phosphate → Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate → 1,3-Bisphosphoglyceric acid → 3-Phosphoglyceric acid → Phosphoenolpyruvate.

Final Answer:
The correct sequence is III → I → V → II → IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER12_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological events of the citric acid cycle

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following biochemical events of the Krebs' (Tricarboxylic Acid) cycle in their correct chronological order starting from the entry of acetyl-CoA into the mitochondrial matrix:

  1. Substrate-level phosphorylation coupled with the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid
  2. Condensation of acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetic acid to yield citric acid
  3. Decarboxylation and dehydrogenation leading to the formation of \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid
  4. Dehydrogenation of succinic acid accompanied by reduction of \(\text{FAD}^+\) to \(\text{FADH}_2\)
  5. Oxidation of malic acid accompanied by reduction of \(\text{NAD}^+\) to regenerate oxaloacetic acid

Select the correct sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Krebs' cycle (citric acid cycle) is a closed cyclic pathway operating in the mitochondrial matrix that achieves complete oxidative decarboxylation of acetyl groups derived from pyruvate.

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of Cycle Events
1. The cycle initiates when the 2-carbon acetyl group of acetyl-CoA condenses with 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA) in the presence of citrate synthase to form 6-carbon citric acid (II).
2. Citrate is isomerised to isocitrate, which undergoes the first oxidative decarboxylation to produce 5-carbon \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid with release of \(\text{CO}_2\) and reduction of \(\text{NAD}^+\) to \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) (III).
3. \(\alpha\)-Ketoglutaric acid undergoes a second oxidative decarboxylation to form succinyl-CoA. Succinyl-CoA is then cleaved to succinic acid coupled with the synthesis of GTP (substrate-level phosphorylation), which transfers its phosphate to ADP forming ATP (I).
4. Succinic acid is oxidized to fumarate (and then malate) by succinate dehydrogenase, transferring electrons to reduce \(\text{FAD}^+\) into \(\text{FADH}_2\) (IV).
5. Finally, malic acid is oxidized to regenerate the initial acceptor molecule oxaloacetic acid, coupled with the reduction of \(\text{NAD}^+\) to \(\text{NADH} + \text{H}^+\) (V).

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
Arranging these events in chronological order from initiation through regeneration gives: II → III → I → IV → V.

Final Answer:
The correct sequence is II → III → I → IV → V.
